title: Alternating omission and the continuous coordinate differential
statement:
Let $E$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a topology making addition, multiplication and inversion on $E\setminus\{0\}$ continuous. Let $J$ be a group with a topology making multiplication and inversion continuous. Let $V$ be an $E$-vector space with a topology making addition and scalar multiplication continuous, and with an $E$-linear $J$-action for which $J\times V\to V$ is continuous. For $n\geq0$ let $B_J^n(V)$ be the space of jointly continuous functions $F:J^{n+1}\to V$ with $F(ax_0,\ldots,ax_n)=aF(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$, and let $C_J^n(V)$ be the space of continuous functions $J^n\to V$, with $C_J^0(V)=V$. All finite powers have the product topology, and both spaces have pointwise operations. Write $P_n(g_1,\ldots,g_n)=(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_n)$ and $r_n(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=(x_0^{-1}x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}^{-1}x_n)$. Put $\Phi_{J,n}F=F\circ P_n$ and $(\Psi_{J,n}f)(x)=x_0f(r_n(x))$, using empty tuples for $n=0$. Define
$$(\delta_J^nF)(x_0,\ldots,x_{n+1})=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^iF(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_{n+1}),$$
$$(d_J^nf)(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{i=1}^{n}(-1)^if(g_1,\ldots,g_ig_{i+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n),$$
with $(d_J^0v)(g)=gv-v$. These formulas give $E$-linear maps $\delta_J^n:B_J^n(V)\to B_J^{n+1}(V)$ and $d_J^n:C_J^n(V)\to C_J^{n+1}(V)$, and $\delta_J^{n+1}\delta_J^n=0$. For every $F\in B_J^n(V)$ one has
$$\Phi_{J,n+1}\delta_J^nF=d_J^n\Phi_{J,n}F.$$
More explicitly, put $p_0=1$, $p_i=g_1\cdots g_i$ for $1\leq i\leq n+1$. The first face is
$$F(p_1,\ldots,p_{n+1})=g_1(\Phi_{J,n}F)(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1});$$
for $1\leq i\leq n$ the $i$-th face is
$$F(p_0,\ldots,\widehat{p_i},\ldots,p_{n+1})=(\Phi_{J,n}F)(g_1,\ldots,g_ig_{i+1},\ldots,g_{n+1}),$$
and the final face is $F(p_0,\ldots,p_n)=(\Phi_{J,n}F)(g_1,\ldots,g_n)$. Their signs are respectively $1$, $(-1)^i$ and $(-1)^{n+1}$. The formulas include $n=0$, when there are no internal faces. No compactness, Hausdorffness or discreteness assumption is made.

proof.text: Pointwise sums and scalar multiples preserve continuity: addition on $V$ is continuous, and $v\mapsto cv$ is continuous for each fixed $c\in E$ by the scalar-multiplication hypothesis. In particular negation is continuous by $c=-1$. The identity $a(cF+c'G)=c(aF)+c'(aG)$ shows that equivariant functions form a vector subspace. Thus the stated pointwise operations define the two $E$-vector spaces, including $C_J^0(V)=V$.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, lines 9007–9040: displayed inhomogeneous differential; elementary agent verification of jointly continuous homogeneous coordinates

proof.text: Each coordinate of $P_n$ is a finite product of coordinate projections, and each coordinate of $r_n$ is an inverse coordinate times the next coordinate; these are continuous by the hypotheses on $J$. Hence $\Phi_{J,n}F$ is continuous. The map $x\mapsto(x_0,f(r_n(x)))$ is continuous, so joint continuity of the action makes $\Psi_{J,n}f$ continuous. Since $(ax_{i-1})^{-1}(ax_i)=x_{i-1}^{-1}x_i$, its value at $ax$ is $(ax_0)f(r_n(x))=a(\Psi_{J,n}f)(x)$. Both coordinate maps preserve pointwise linear combinations. For $n=0$ these are $F\mapsto F(1)$ and $v\mapsto(x_0\mapsto x_0v)$.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, lines 9007–9040: displayed inhomogeneous differential; elementary agent verification of jointly continuous homogeneous coordinates

proof.text: Deleting a coordinate is continuous for the product topology. Therefore every summand of $\delta_J^nF$ is continuous, as is their finite sum. Deletion commutes with simultaneous left multiplication, so $\delta_J^nF(ax)=\sum_i(-1)^iaF(x\text{ with }i\text{ omitted})=a\delta_J^nF(x)$ by linearity of the action. Distributing finite sums over pointwise linear combinations proves that $\delta_J^n$ is $E$-linear into $B_J^{n+1}(V)$.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, lines 9007–9040: displayed inhomogeneous differential; elementary agent verification of jointly continuous homogeneous coordinates

proof.text: In the formula for $d_J^nf$, dropping an argument is a product projection and merging two adjacent arguments is continuous multiplication in that coordinate. The first term is the composite of $g\mapsto(g_1,f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1}))$ with the jointly continuous action. Thus every term and the finite signed sum are continuous. The action maps are $E$-linear, so distribution through this same formula proves $E$-linearity of $d_J^n$. For $n=0$, $g\mapsto gv-v$ is continuous by the action and addition hypotheses, and linear in $v$.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, lines 9007–9040: displayed inhomogeneous differential; elementary agent verification of jointly continuous homogeneous coordinates

proof.text: Evaluate $\delta_J^{n+1}\delta_J^nF$ on $(x_0,\ldots,x_{n+2})$ and expand the two finite sums. Fix original positions $a<b$. Omitting $a$ first and then position $b-1$ contributes $(-1)^{a+b-1}F(x\text{ with }a,b\text{ omitted})$; omitting $b$ first and then position $a$ contributes $(-1)^{a+b}F(x\text{ with }a,b\text{ omitted})$. These sum to zero, since the two signs differ by a factor of $-1$. Every ordered pair of omissions belongs to exactly one such pair indexed by $a<b$. Regrouping the finite sum proves $\delta_J^{n+1}\delta_J^nF=0$. This works in characteristic two as well: there the equal signs sum to zero.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, lines 9007–9040: displayed inhomogeneous differential; elementary agent verification of jointly continuous homogeneous coordinates

proof.text: For the first face, the tuple $(p_1,\ldots,p_{n+1})$ is $g_1$ times $P_n(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})$ coordinate by coordinate: its $j$th entry is $g_1(g_2\cdots g_{j+1})$, with empty product $1$ when $j=0$. Equivariance of $F$ therefore gives $F(p_1,\ldots,p_{n+1})=g_1(\Phi_{J,n}F)(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})$. Its omission index is $0$, so its sign is $+1$.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, lines 9007–9040: displayed inhomogeneous differential; elementary agent verification of jointly continuous homogeneous coordinates

proof.text: Fix $1\leq i\leq n$ and merge $g_i,g_{i+1}$ into $g_ig_{i+1}$. The cumulative product at position $j<i$ is still $p_j$. At every position $j\geq i$ it is $g_1\cdots g_{i-1}(g_ig_{i+1})g_{i+2}\cdots g_{j+1}=p_{j+1}$, by associativity, without commuting any factors. Thus its cumulative-product tuple is precisely $(p_0,\ldots,\widehat{p_i},\ldots,p_{n+1})$. Applying $F$ gives the claimed internal-face equality, with the unchanged omission sign $(-1)^i$.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology, lines 9007–9040: displayed inhomogeneous differential; elementary agent verification of jointly continuous homogeneous coordinates

proof.text: Dropping the last coordinate of $(p_0,\ldots,p_{n+1})$ leaves exactly $P_n(g_1,\ldots,g_n)$, so the last face is the claimed value with sign $(-1)^{n+1}$. Substitute this and the previous two face calculations into the defining finite sum for $(\delta_J^nF)(P_{n+1}(g))$. The result is exactly $(d_J^n\Phi_{J,n}F)(g)$; equality at every $g$ proves the asserted identity of functions. When $n=0$ the tuple is $(1,g)$, the two values are $F(g)=gF(1)$ and $F(1)$, and there are no internal faces: the sum is $gF(1)-F(1)$ as required.
